previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted with right-sided testicular pain and swelling, presenting with fever and leukocytosis. He was diagnosed with febrile epididymo-orchitis, supported by scrotal ultrasound showing right testicular inflammation and a complex hydrocele likely representing a pyocele. He was treated with IV cefepime initially, with improvement in symptoms and white blood cell count. Urine cultures grew E. coli resistant to ciprofloxacin and Bactrim, and pan-sensitive Proteus, both sensitive to cephalosporins. He remained afebrile, and his renal function and potassium normalized. He was discharged on oral cefpodoxime for a 14-day course, with updated warfarin dosing and instructions to follow up with his urologist and primary care provider. His chronic conditions, including heart failure, diabetes, cirrhosis, and anticoagulation, were managed without complication.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man s/p ERCP with mass resection ___, now w/ ___
abdominal pain, involuntary guarding// Eval for free air

TECHNIQUE:  Supine and upright abdominal radiographs were obtained.

COMPARISON:  Abdominal radiograph ___, CT abdomen ___

FINDINGS: 

A mid sternotomy wire and a pacemaker with defibrillator lead projects in the
upper midline of the radiograph.

There are no abnormally dilated loops of large or small bowel.  There is
moderate fecal load and gas throughout the colon. Relative hypodensities
lateral to the spleen and liver likely reflect fat deposition as seen on the
prior CT.
There is no definite free intraperitoneal air.

Multiple round radiodensities are seen in the left kidney shadow corresponding
to known left renal stones seen on prior CT.  Vascular calcification of both
iliac arteries.
Degenerative changes in the lumbar spine and both hips, greater on the right.

IMPRESSION: 

No definite evidence of free peritoneal air.  Nonobstructive gas pattern.

EXAMINATION:  CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis without and with intravenous
contrast

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with gastric adenocarcinoma s/p resection//
staging CT with po and IV contrast

TECHNIQUE:  Oncology 3 phase: Multidetector CT of the abdomen and pelvis was
done as part of CT torso without and with IV contrast. Initially the abdomen
was scanned without IV contrast. Subsequently a single bolus of IV contrast
was injected and the abdomen and pelvis were scanned in the portal venous
phase, followed by a scan of the abdomen in equilibrium (3-min delay) phase.
Oral contrast was administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

HEPATOBILIARY: Morphologic features of cirrhosis.  Subcentimeter hypodense

dilatation. Uncomplicated cholelithiasis.

PANCREAS: Unremarkable.

SPLEEN: 14 mm hypodense lesion within the spleen, likely sequelae of prior
infarction.

ADRENALS: The adrenal glands are unremarkable.

URINARY: 30 mm simple cyst arising from the upper pole of the left kidney. 
Additional 9 mm hypodense lesion within the interpolar region of the right
kidney is too small to characterize but appears hyperdense on the unenhanced

nephrolithiasis, left greater than right.  Bilateral kidneys demonstrate areas
of cortical thinning and atrophy, particularly involving the right lower pole.
No hydronephrosis.

GASTROINTESTINAL: The known gastric malignancy is not identified.  Ectopic
pancreatic tissue is again seen in the second stage of the duodenum.  There is
no bowel obstruction or ascites.

LYMPH NODES: No retroperitoneal or mesenteric adenopathy. No pelvic or
inguinal adenopathy.

VASCULAR: Fusiform ectasia of the infrarenal abdominal aorta measuring up to
29 mm.  Moderate atherosclerotic calcification.

BONES: Grade 1 anterolisthesis of L4 on L5.  Sclerotic lesion within the right
iliac bone is stable from ___, likely a small bone island.  Degenerative
changes of bilateral hips.  No suspicious osseous lesion.

SOFT TISSUES: Small bilateral fat containing inguinal hernias.

2. Redemonstration of hepatic cirrhosis.
